105	**D154 — DEVDESK-486: on native Windows the path trace sends ICMP echo requests through `IcmpSendEcho2`, not UDP probes. Decided (user, 2026-11-15): (1) On windows/amd64 (and the other Windows architectures once measured), `internal/nettrace` runs one `IcmpSendEcho2` call (`iphlpapi.dll`, synchronous) per TTL, each in its own goroutine, as D143 does for its sockets. The call takes no admin rights: it is what `tracert.exe` uses. The Linux design of D143 (UDP to port 33435, `IP_RECVERR`) is unchanged. (2) "Reached" on Windows means an Echo Reply from the target, not a Port Unreachable. A router's Time Exceeded ends nothing; a Destination Unreachable from a router still ends the trace as `HopUnreachable`, as on Linux. (3) Classification is by error code, never by text: the `IP_STATUS` values of `ipexport.h` and the `windows.Errno` values, never the localized message (D20). `IsNoRoute` now recognises `WSAENETUNREACH`, `WSAEHOSTUNREACH`, `ERROR_NETWORK_UNREACHABLE` and `ERROR_HOST_UNREACHABLE`. *Refines point 5 of D151: a proof of "no route" now exists on Windows; macOS stays `undetermined`.* (4) A Windows `IP_SUCCESS` from an address other than the target still counts as the target: an echo reply comes only from the destination's own stack. Linux's stricter source check is not mirrored. (5) Windows Firewall: Time Exceeded and Echo Reply to our outgoing echoes pass without any rule and without admin, as with `tracert`. A third-party firewall can make hops silent; that is not detected. Measured on Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300 (dev machine), amd64: a live trace to `1.1.1.1` reached the target in 15 hops; TTL 1, 2 and 8 answered as routers, the other intermediate hops stayed silent, and no firewall error appeared. windows/arm64 and 386 are not measured; the struct layout is pinned by `TestEchoReplyLayout`. (6) Source guard: `source_guard_test.go` now covers `golang.org/x/sys/windows`. Calls to `NewLazySystemDLL` and `NewProc` are allowlisted; writes to `Name`, `System` and `Dll` are refused. Known residual: `reflect`, `unsafe`, `go:linkname` and `cgo` are not covered by an AST guard. Consequences and gaps: a target that filters ICMP echo stays silent although it would answer UDP, and the reverse; the same target can give different hop lists from the Windows host and from WSL2 (WSL2 keeps the Linux UDP engine). Rejected: (a) asynchronous `IcmpSendEcho2` (`Icmp6SendEcho2` ignores the timeout in async mode, the reply buffer must stay pinned, and cancelling is not documented); (b) raw sockets (need admin); (c) shelling out to `tracert.exe` (forbidden by the source guard, and its output is localized). Out of scope, split into their own stories: IPv6 (`Icmp6SendEcho2` on Windows, `IPV6_UNICAST_HOPS` and `IPV6_RECVERR` on Linux), and macOS. Why: no admin, the same mechanism as `tracert`, and error codes that do not depend on the Windows language. No ADR: local to `internal/nettrace` and reversible by a revert. **Plane:** DEVDESK-486 (story), dated 2026-11-15. Sources: `internal/nettrace/trace_windows.go`, `noroute_windows.go`, `echo_status.go`, `echo_conn.go`, `source_guard_test.go`, `live_windows_test.go` (worktree `.worktrees/feat-486-windows-path-trace`, branch `feat/486-windows-path-trace`, uncommitted when this entry was written); D20, D143, D151.**
106	
107	**D153 — DEVDESK-471 (P2-02): the Path tab is removed; the path trace survives only as the trace level of Diagnostics. Decided (user, 2026-11-15): (1) The network view has four tabs: Diagnostics, Ports, Interfaces, Forward. *Supersedes point 1 of D144 (Path as the fifth tab).* (2) `H` on the Local route row opens the trace level on the results' target, in the ready state, and never starts a trace. `enter` starts it. D144 point 4 stands, its "Path tab" now read as this trace level. (3) Inside the trace level, `enter` starts a trace and also restarts it ("Trace again") once a trace has ended or been cancelled. `ctrl+o` opens "Trace from", a declared keymap exception (`netdiag/trace`, replacing `netdiag/path`). `esc` cancels a running trace, then returns to the origin screen (form or results) with its state. *Supersedes point 2 of D152 (no `ctrl+o` and no relaunch in the sub-level).* (4) `PathModel` has no target field: the target comes from the form, entered once. *Ends the cost accepted in point 1 of D152.* (5) `H` and Trace Path are greyed, with their reason, on a platform that cannot trace and on a target the trace refuses (for example an IPv6 literal). (6) Changing the source returns to the ready state and starts nothing. (7) `esc` on the prefilled form opened from Status is unchanged: it does nothing, as today (AC6, option b). Hypotheses: H1 to H7 of the plan, prudent defaults, not validated. Out of scope, tracked in Plane as DEVDESK-485: the cursor blink of the Diagnostics form is lost after `restoreFormFocus` and `moveFocus`, because the `Cmd` returned by `Focus()` is dropped; it predates this change for `moveFocus`. Why: one trace surface, no duplicated target field, and the trace stays opt-in (D144 point 4). No ADR: local and reversible by a revert. **Plane:** DEVDESK-471. Sources: `.claude/plans/devdesk-471-remove-path-tab-plan.md`, D144, D150 point 5, D152, the audit `.claude/plans/net-view-ux-audit.md` (option P2).**
108	
109	**D152 — DEVDESK-470: the Diagnostics form gets a Trace Path sub-level that reuses the Path tab's engine. Decided (user, 2026-11-15): (1) The sub-level of the Diagnostics form runs on the single `m.pathModel` instance, not a second one. A second instance would accept `pathResolvedMsg`, `pathHopMsg` and `pathDoneMsg` (which carry only the generation, with counters at 0) in both places. Cost, accepted: the target field of the Path tab receives the form's target, as `H` does, and any text being typed there is overwritten, until P2-02 (removal of the Path tab). *Ended by D153 point 4.* (2) No `ctrl+o` and no relaunch inside the sub-level: to relaunch, `esc` then activate Trace Path again. *Superseded by D153 point 3: `ctrl+o` and `enter` (relaunch) work inside the trace level.* (3) `enter` on a text field always runs Run Diagnostics; a trace starts only from its button. (4) When Port or DNS Server is filled in, the trace runs on the target alone, with an Info notice in the footer. (5) The refusal of Run Diagnostics is unchanged (a timed error, no underline). Only Trace Path applies Rule 140 (invalid field underlined, error also in the footer). (6) The Trace Path button is greyed, with its reason in the footer permanently, when the platform does not support the trace (DEVDESK-334). Reference: D150 point 5 (the net view redesign, option P2, comes after DEVDESK-335). Why: one engine, one generation counter, so the two views cannot answer for each other. No ADR: local and reversible. **Plane:** DEVDESK-470, decided by the maintainer on 2026-11-15. Shipped with DEVDESK-470. Sources: `internal/ui/netdiag/trace_form.go`, `trace_level.go`, `.claude/plans/net-view-ux-audit.md`, D150, D151.**
110

560	`persistentvolumeclaims`; create `pods/exec` (used by `Provision`); list `services` in all namespaces (NodePort check).
561	
562	**Not covered by the fakes.** `Deploy` has only run against a scripted `Runner`,
563	a fake `Prober` and a fake `Clock`; the real kubectl output shape of
564	`get pods -o json` (container status fields), the real duration of the pull and
565	the start, and whether `kubectl apply --server-side` of a Namespace that carries
566	no field of its own conflicts on a second run were left for step 10: the real
567	output was read, a second `up` applied the same two documents with no conflict,
568	and the start took 48 s (see "First real run").
569	
570	## Residual risks (security audit of the steps 4, 6, 7)
571	
572	Known and accepted for a throw-away bench; none is fixed by this change.
573	
574	- **Basic credentials in clear HTTP.** Nexus is reached on `http://`, so the admin
575	  and `bench-pull` credentials of `Provision` travel unencrypted. The command
576	  honours the commitment made for it: it sends them to
577	  `RESTBaseURL("127.0.0.1", p)` and to another host only on `--rest-host`, with a
578	  warning (see "The command"). The package itself does not enforce it.
579	- **`local-path` volume in `0777`.** The data folder of the local-path
580	  provisioner is world-writable, so `admin.password` is readable by every local
581	  account of the node between the start of Nexus and the provisioning (which
582	  changes it).
583	- **NodePorts on the LAN, anonymous access on purpose.** The two NodePorts listen
584	  on every interface of the node, and anonymous access is enabled by default so
585	  that pulls need no login (`NEXUS_BENCH_ANONYMOUS`). Anyone on the LAN can read
586	  the bench; do not put anything private in it.
587	- **Mutable image tag.** The image is `docker.io/sonatype/nexus3:<tag>` with no
588	  digest: the same tag can resolve to another image later.
589	- **Partial result on error.** `Provision` returns the `ProvisionResult` it had
590	  gathered together with the error. The command does not write the descriptor
591	  when `err != nil` (`TestDescriptorIsNotWrittenUnlessProvisionSucceeded`), or it
592	  would describe a bench that is half provisioned.
593	
594	## The command and the mise tasks (`cmd/nexus-bench`, `mise.toml`)
595	
596	`internal/nexusbench/cmd/nexus-bench` is a `package main` of five files:
597	`main.go` (`deps`, `defaultDeps`, `run`), `flags.go` (flags and parameter
598	resolution), `commands.go` (`up`, `provision`, `down`, `render`), `status.go` and
599	`usage.go` (the help). `main()` only builds a context cancelled by SIGINT and
600	SIGTERM, calls `run(ctx, args, os.Getenv, os.Stdout, os.Stderr, defaultDeps())`
601	and exits with its code. `deps` holds every constructor and library call that
602	reaches a cluster (`newRunner`, `newProber`, `clock`, `newStore`, `newInitial`,
603	`preflight`, `deploy`, `provision`, `destroy`); `defaultDeps` wires
604	`NewExecRunner`, `NewProber`, `NewClock`, `NewFileStore`,
605	`NewKubectlInitialPassword`, `RunPreflight`, `Deploy`, `Provision` and `Destroy`,
606	and the tests wire fakes, so no test needs kubectl or a network.
607	
608	**Tasks.** Six, in `mise.toml`, none reachable from `ci`, `check`, `test` or
609	`test-race` (`mise_tasks_test.go` reads the file and checks it, and checks that
610	`kubectl` is declared on each of them, not in the global `[tools]`, so the CI does
611	not install it; kubectl `1.35`, because `datomir` runs k0s v1.36.x and kubectl is
612	supported within one minor version of the API server, so 1.35 is the oldest
613	accepted; `render` contacts no cluster and declares no kubectl, and the test
614	requires its absence there). Arguments follow `--`: mise appends them to the
615	command line.
616	
617	| Task | Runs | Acts on the cluster |
618	|---|---|---|
619	| `nexus-bench:up` | `go run ./internal/nexusbench/cmd/nexus-bench up` | yes |
620	| `nexus-bench:provision` | `... provision` | yes (REST and `exec`) |
621	| `nexus-bench:down` | `... down` | yes (deletes the namespace) |
622	| `nexus-bench:status` | `... status` | reads only |
623	| `nexus-bench:render` | `... render` | no, contacts nothing |
624	| `nexus-bench:test` | `go test -timeout 60m -count=1 -run Integration ./internal/nexusbench/...` with `DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH=1` set by the task's `env` table (portable, no `env` command) | yes; the tests skip when `CI` is set |
625	
626	**Subcommands and flags.** Every subcommand takes the same parameter flags, one
627	per `NEXUS_BENCH_*` variable: `--context`, `--namespace`, `--http-nodeport`,
628	`--docker-nodeport`, `--cpu-request`, `--cpu-limit`, `--memory-request`,
629	`--memory-limit`, `--storage-size`, `--jvm-opts`, `--image`, `--image-tag`,
630	`--upstream-url`, `--anonymous`, `--hosts`, `--timeout`, `--delete-timeout`,
631	`--secrets`, `--descriptor`. `up` and `provision` add `--accept-eula` and
632	`--rest-host`. Each subcommand has its own `flag.FlagSet` (`ContinueOnError`,
633	output discarded: the command prints parse errors itself on stderr and `-h` on
634	stdout). A flag is laid over its variable and the result goes through
635	`FromEnv(Defaults(), ...)` once, so "flag, then `NEXUS_BENCH_*`, then default",
636	the parsing and the rule that `--namespace` moves the upstream URL (unless an
637	upstream is given, by flag or variable) are the library's own. `--accept-eula`
638	becomes `yes` (and `--accept-eula=false` `no`, which beats a variable set to
639	`yes`). `Validate` runs before anything else, `render` included.
640	
641	**Exit codes.** `0` success; `1` failure (invalid parameter, kubectl missing, a
642	step failed, a run cancelled); `2` mistake in the command line (no or unknown
643	subcommand, unknown flag, a value of the wrong type, a missing value, an extra
644	argument), with the help on stderr when the subcommand is missing or unknown.
645	`help`, `-h` and `--help` print on stdout and exit `0`. `go run` (so every
646	`mise run nexus-bench:*`) does not propagate the code: it prints `exit status 2`
647	and exits `1`. Code `2` is only visible when the compiled binary is run directly;
648	the general help says so (`TestHelpSaysGoRunDoesNotKeepExitCodeTwo`).
649	
650	**Interruption.** `main()` cancels the run's context on SIGINT or SIGTERM and
651	then hands the signals back to the default behavior (`context.AfterFunc(ctx,
652	stop)`), so a second Ctrl-C kills a run that is slow to wind down. This is not
653	unit-tested: it lives in `main()`, which the tests do not call.
654	
655	**Output.** The progress of the library steps goes to stdout, then one line
656	`nexus-bench: descriptor written to <path>`. Every failure is one line on stderr:
657	a `BenchError` (also when wrapped by `%w` or joined) prints exactly its
658	`Error()`, and nothing around it or inside it (no wrapper text, no `Err`, no
659	trace); a cancelled run says `cancelled` and that `status` shows where things
660	stand; another error prints its message. No output holds a password
661	(`requireClean` of the tests plants markers in the fakes).
662	
663	**`up`.** Resolve the parameters, then the secrets path
664	(`--secrets`/`NEXUS_BENCH_SECRETS`, else `DefaultSecretsPath`; with no place for
665	it the run stops before any cluster call and says to set
666	`NEXUS_BENCH_SECRETS`), `newRunner`, `newStore` (the git guard), `Deploy` (which
667	runs `RunPreflight(OpUp)` itself, so the command does not run a second one), then
668	`Provision`, then the descriptor. **The descriptor is written only after a
669	successful `Provision`**, never on a failure at any step, and a descriptor from
670	an earlier run is left as it was. It is built with `BuildDescriptor(p,
671	DeployResult, ProvisionResult)`.
672	
673	**`provision`.** `RunPreflight(OpProvision)`, `Provision`, then the descriptor,
674	built with `DeployResult{NodeIP: <node address of the preflight>}`.
675	
676	**`down`.** `Destroy` (its own `RunPreflight(OpDown)` first). The descriptor is
677	not touched or created.
678	
679	**`status`.** Read-only: `RunPreflight(OpStatus)` (a missing namespace is its
680	`NamespaceMissing` error, exit `1`), one `kubectl get pods -l
681	app.kubernetes.io/name=nexus -o json`, one probe of the REST origin, one read of
682	the descriptor. Four lines, each a finding, exit `0`:
683	
684	    bench: namespace nexus-bench, context datomir
685	    pod: running (nexus-xxx, 1/1 ready, 0 restarts)     | not found | pending ...
686	    rest: ready (http://127.0.0.1:30481)                 | not ready (the cause is not shown)
687	    descriptor: matches (<path>) | not found (<path>) | differs from the current parameters (<path>) + one line per field
688	
689	The comparison covers context, namespace, image, both NodePorts, the upstream URL
690	and the anonymous flag; hosts and versions come from the cluster and are left out.
691	It creates no store, builds no `InitialPassword` and sends no credential.
692	
693	**`render`.** Prints `Render(p)` and nothing else; it builds no dependency (the
694	test runs it with an empty `deps`).
695	
696	**Where the credentials go.** `Provision` is given
697	`RESTBaseURL("127.0.0.1", p)`, whatever hosts `Deploy` reached, so the admin and
698	`bench-pull` passwords stay on the loopback by default. `--rest-host <host>`
699	(a host name, an IPv4 or IPv6 address, brackets and a zone allowed; no port,
700	scheme, path, credentials or space, refused before any cluster call with exit
701	`1`) sends them to that host instead, and unless it is a loopback address or
702	`localhost` the command prints on stderr a warning that the credentials travel in
703	clear text. `status` and the deployment wait probe without credentials.
704	
705	**Non-default bench.** After writing the descriptor, if the parameters differ
706	from `Defaults()` (any field but the two timeouts, the two paths, the EULA
707	consent and an empty host list), stderr gets `warning: descriptor.json now
708	describes a non-default bench; do not commit it`. The file is written all the
709	same, at `--descriptor`/`NEXUS_BENCH_DESCRIPTOR`, else the versioned one. A
710	default bench prints nothing on stderr.
711	
712	## Integration tests and source guards (`bench_integration_test.go`, `guard_test.go`, step 9)
713	
714	Read-only state of the run on 2026-11-16: the three read tests pass (8 subtests)
715	and the lifecycle passes (151 s for two downs and three deployments).
716	
717	**Gates.** Every test of `bench_integration_test.go` starts with
718	`requireBench(t)`: it skips unless `DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH=1` and `CI` is empty, so
719	`mise run test`, `check`, `ci` and the CI never reach the cluster. The mise task
720	`nexus-bench:test` sets the variable (`env` table). The destructive test needs
721	two more things: `DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH_LIFECYCLE=1` and `NEXUS_BENCH_ACCEPT_EULA=yes`
722	(the lifecycle provisions Nexus, so the EULA has to be accepted by the operator).
723	None of the tests writes the versioned `descriptor.json`.
724	
725	**The four tests.** The first three need a bench that is up and provisioned
726	(`mise run nexus-bench:up`): they read the versioned descriptor and the secrets
727	file (`openLiveBench`; the REST URL is the descriptor's one on the loopback) and
728	fail with the command to run when either is missing.
729	
730	| Test | Reads | Writes |
731	|---|---|---|
732	| `TestIntegrationBenchDescribed` | `GET /service/rest/v1/status` without credentials (200), then as admin the repository list and, per repository of the descriptor, its type, format, group members or proxy remote URL | nothing |
733	| `TestIntegrationAnonymousAsDescribed` | the anonymous-access setting as admin, and `GET /repositories` without credentials: 200 when the descriptor says anonymous is enabled, 401 when not | nothing |
734	| `TestIntegrationPullAccountIsReadOnly` | `GET /repositories` as `bench-pull` (200) | one control `POST` of a hosted repository `bench-readonly-probe` as `bench-pull`, which has to be refused with **403**. If Nexus accepts it (any 2xx), the test deletes that repository as admin and fails |
735	| `TestIntegrationLifecycle` | admin listings of repositories, roles and users | destructive, see below |
736	
737	`TestIntegrationLifecycle` runs `Deploy` and `Provision` (first up), compares a
738	snapshot of repositories, roles and users, runs up and provision a second time
739	and requires the same snapshot (idempotence), then `Destroy` and checks that
740	`get namespace` answers NotFound, `Deploy` on a fresh instance (the pod must hold
741	an `admin.password` again), and a final `Destroy`. It uses the parameters of
742	`FromEnv` and the secrets path of the bench (`NEXUS_BENCH_SECRETS`, else the
743	default), refuses to start without the EULA, and refuses when `go test` has less
744	than 45 minutes left (`lifecycleMinTimeout`: three deployments of up to ten
745	minutes plus the deletions; the default of `go test` is 10 minutes). The
746	namespace is whatever the parameters say; the preflight already refuses a
747	namespace this tool did not create.
748	
749	**Running it.** The task passes `-timeout 60m` for that reason
750	(`TestMiseBenchTestTaskRunsTheIntegrationTestsGuarded` requires a `-timeout` of
751	at least 45 minutes):
752	
753	    mise run nexus-bench:test                         # the three read tests, lifecycle skipped
754	    DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH_LIFECYCLE=1 NEXUS_BENCH_ACCEPT_EULA=yes mise run nexus-bench:test
755	
756	**A failure leaves the bench deployed.** The lifecycle uses `t.Fatalf` and no
757	cleanup: when a step fails halfway, the namespace stays as it is so that the
758	cause can be diagnosed (`nexus-bench status`, `kubectl logs`). Clean up with
759	`mise run nexus-bench:down`.
760	
761	**Source guards (`guard_test.go`).** Three tests read the package with
762	`go/parser`, name file and line, and each detector has a self-test fed with a
763	faulty and a correct source held in memory. A failure points at code that breaks
764	the rule, not at a test to relax.
765	
766	1. *Every test that reaches the bench calls `requireBench(t)` first.* A call of
767	   `NewExecRunner`, `DescriptorPath`, `DefaultSecretsPath` or `newClient` (unless
768	   `newClient` is given the address of an `httptest` server) before the guard, or
769	   in a function without it, fails. Exceptions are named in
770	   `requireBenchExceptions`, with a `check` that verifies the reason in the
771	   source (the PATH is isolated, the environment is a map); an exception that
772	   matches nothing fails too (`TestGuardExceptionsStillMatch`). Limit: calls are
773	   read by name in the test files of this folder; a call hidden behind a function
774	   value, or made by the tests of `cmd/nexus-bench` (which run on fakes), is not
775	   seen.
776	2. *Only `kubectl.go` and `secrets.go` start a process* (`exec.Command` or
777	   `CommandContext`, any import name, dot import refused): one door to the
778	   cluster, one to `git check-ignore`. A listed file that no longer starts one
779	   must be dropped from the list. Limit: `syscall.Exec`, `os.StartProcess` and a
780	   process started by another package are not seen.
781	3. *No Authorization header outside the client.* The word `authorization` (in an
782	   identifier or a string) may appear only in `nexusapi.go` and `probe.go`,
783	   `SetBasicAuth` only in `nexusapi.go`, and `net/http/httputil` is imported
784	   nowhere. Comments are not read. Limit: a header name built by concatenation,
785	   or a whole `http.Header` printed with `%v`, is not seen.
786	
787	**The mise guard** (`mise_tasks_test.go`) reads `mise.toml` with a small
788	line-based reader (no TOML library in `go.mod`) and checks: the six tasks exist
789	and call the command; none of `ci`, `check`, `test`, `test-race` reaches a
790	`nexus-bench` task, directly or through `depends` and `run` references; `kubectl`
791	is declared on `up`, `provision`, `down`, `status` and `test`, absent on `render`
792	and absent from the global `[tools]`; `nexus-bench:test` sets
793	`DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH=1`, runs `-run Integration` and carries a `-timeout` of at
794	least 45 minutes. Limit: it reads the file, it does not ask mise to resolve it.
795	
796	## First real run (datomir, 2026-11-16)
797	
798	Step 10, on k0s v1.36 (`datomir`), image `docker.io/sonatype/nexus3:3.98.1`
799	(pulled in 10.6 s), `Server: Nexus/3.98.1-01 (COMMUNITY)`. The operator accepted
800	the Community EULA before the run; the REST client never accepts it on its own.
801	
802	**Deployment (H-RES).** First `up` on an empty cluster namespace: 48 s from the
803	apply to a Ready pod and a changed admin password (pull included); the pod went
804	Pending, ContainerCreating, running not ready, ready, and the claim bound with
805	the pod (`local-path`). Idle after provisioning: 55m CPU and 1257Mi memory
806	(`kubectl top pod`), against the 3Gi request and 4Gi limit of D-C: the request
807	could be lowered, but it was kept (the JVM grows with the first pulls, to be
808	measured with NX-02). `/nexus-data` held 3.7 MB. `admin.password` is gone once
809	the password is changed through the API (H-REST confirmed). An `up` on an
810	already provisioned namespace takes 1 to 2 s.
811	
812	**REST statuses seen** (Nexus `request.log`): `PUT .../users/admin/change-password`
813	204, `POST /system/eula` 204, `PUT /security/realms/active` 204, `PUT
814	/security/anonymous` 200, `POST /security/roles` 200, `POST /security/users`
815	200, `POST /repositories/docker/hosted` 201, `POST .../group` 201, `PUT
816	/security/roles/{id}` 204, `PUT /security/users/{id}` 204, `PUT
817	.../users/{id}/change-password` 204, `PUT .../hosted/{name}` and `PUT
818	.../group/{name}` 204. The swagger lists the same codes (`GET /v1/system/eula`
819	answers 200 whatever the state, `POST` 204/500). The client accepts any 2xx; the
820	fake answers 200 for `POST` roles and users and 201 for repositories, as the
821	swagger and the instance do.
822	
823	**The proxy.** `POST /repositories/docker/proxy` with
824	`http://bench-upstream.nexus-bench.svc.cluster.local:5000`, a host that does not
825	exist yet (NX-02): `400`, content type `application/vnd.siesta-validation-errors-v1+json`,
826	body `[{"id":"HelperBean.proxy.remoteUrl","message":"Proxy URL blocked: Failed to
827	resolve host: ..."}]`. The proxy is not created, the instance keeps working. The
828	answer to this is in "REST client and provisioning", step 9: the proxy is
829	pending, the group holds `docker-hosted` alone, the descriptor says so. The
830	committed `descriptor.json` therefore describes the bench as it is before NX-02:
831	`docker-hosted` and `docker-group` (with `docker-hosted` as its only member), no
832	proxy. It is not the descriptor of the bench after NX-02, which has the proxy and
833	lists it in the group, so the versioned file differs before and after NX-02. It
834	also embeds the node IP `192.168.1.31`, which is specific to this machine.
835	
836	**CA2 (REST provisioning) is met for `docker-hosted` and `docker-group`; the
837	proxy is deferred to NX-02.** Nexus 3.98.1-01 refuses a proxy whose upstream host
838	does not resolve, and the upstream only exists once NX-02 deploys it. The
839	criterion to carry into NX-02: run `mise run nexus-bench:up` again, check that
840	`docker-proxy` exists and is a member of `docker-group`, and commit the new
841	`descriptor.json`.
842	
843	**Idempotence (CA3).** A second and third `up` sent no `POST` but the refused
844	proxy one (the pending proxy of "The proxy" above), `PUT` everything else (including a `change-password` of `bench-pull`
845	with the stored password, the same value), left every password unchanged and
846	wrote byte for byte the same `descriptor.json`. The lifecycle test compares the
847	snapshots of repositories, roles and users after a second up and provision and
848	finds them equal.
849	
850	**Read-only tests.** `TestIntegrationBenchDescribed`,
851	`TestIntegrationAnonymousAsDescribed` and `TestIntegrationPullAccountIsReadOnly`
852	pass: status 200 without credentials, the anonymous settings and the anonymous
853	`GET /repositories` as described, and the control `POST` of `bench-pull` is
854	refused with 403 (nothing was created).
855	
856	**Lifecycle (CA3, CA4).** `TestIntegrationLifecycle` passes in 151 s: up,
857	provision, up and provision again with no change, `down`, `up` on a fresh
858	instance (a new pod with a new `admin.password`), `down`. Afterwards the namespace
859	is `NotFound`, no PersistentVolume of the bench remains (`local-path` reclaims
860	with `Delete`), `secrets.json` is removed (the empty `datomir` folder above it
861	stays) and `descriptor.json` is unchanged.
862	
863	## Still to come
864	
865	NX-02 deploys the upstream (`bench-upstream` in the bench namespace); after it,
866	`mise run nexus-bench:up` creates the proxy, puts it into the group, and the
867	descriptor gets the proxy back (CA2 for the proxy; commit the new `descriptor.json`). This file grows with each step.
868

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only) + a path trace under Diagnostics (Trace Path button, or `H` on the route row; no separate tab since DEVDESK-471) (native path trace, on native Linux, native Windows (IPv4 only, ICMP echoes through `iphlpapi`, DEVDESK-486) and WSL2: on macOS and WSL1 the button, `H`, `enter` and `ctrl+o` are greyed and the footer says why, DEVDESK-334; the column starts with this machine, its interface and its gateway; `ctrl+o` can start it from a running Docker Engine container instead (container and network rows, hops still traced from this machine); `H` on the Diagnostics route row opens the trace level on that host without starting it (greyed with the reason on an unsupported platform or a target the trace refuses; its interface and gateway rows reuse the Local route check's reading of the same address, read once, DEVDESK-473), and in the trace level `enter` starts or restarts it, `ctrl+o` picks the source, `esc` cancels then goes back where it came from; under WSL2 the source row says `WSL2 (VM), not the Windows host` with the networking mode, and in NAT mode the gateway and TTL 1 hop are tagged `Windows host (virtual switch)` only when proven, DEVDESK-333; the interface row says `no route` when the kernel proves there is none and `undetermined` when the routing table could not be read, a no-route error keeps the local rows, a trace that ends on the hop limit or the deadline folds its silent tail into one `silent` row and marks the `last to answer` hop, and the target refuses a `:port`, DEVDESK-335)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
mise run ci           # the six checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. CI itself runs only fmt-check, vet, lint and build: tests are disabled in CI (maintainer decision, D149), so run this locally before every PR

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

## Architecture

The deep notes live in `docs/architecture/`, one file per area, and they are
**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are
touching, and update it in the same commit as the code.

| [`configuration.md`](../docs/architecture/configuration.md) | the config schema, the contexts, the migrations (`gitlab:` → `forge:`, `docker:` → `network:`), `agent_usage.prices`, and the configuration view |
| [`forge.md`](../docs/architecture/forge.md) | `internal/forge` and its two backends, `forge.Vocabulary`, the explorer's clone pipeline, and how the explorer reads the forge index (`internal/forgeindex`) and its `g` |
| [`workspaces.md`](../docs/architecture/workspaces.md) | the `ws` file icons (`internal/ui/fileicon`) and the sync (`F`) |
| [`filebrowser.md`](../docs/architecture/filebrowser.md) | `:files` (`internal/ui/filebrowser`, `internal/fsbrowse`), the path picker a form's path field opens with enter, and `theme.ShortPath` |

| [`scanning.md`](../docs/architecture/scanning.md) | Trivy, Gitleaks, plumber, `scan.Categorize`, the `:sec` inventory, the two scan caches, image signatures (`internal/trust`, the cosign verifier) |
| [`registries.md`](../docs/architecture/registries.md) | the registry/group model and the discovered-members cache |
| [`network.md`](../docs/architecture/network.md) | `internal/docker` and `internal/oci` (typed `StatusError`, `...Context` variants), `internal/imagesearch` and the registry browser's image search level, image updates (`internal/imageupdate`, the Update column), verified pulls (`internal/imagepull`), the netdiag view, `internal/ports`, `internal/netiface`, `internal/nettrace` (the path trace: unprivileged UDP + `IP_RECVERR` on Linux, ICMP echo through `iphlpapi` on native Windows) |

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Dependencies

Go 1.27 (`go 1.27.3` in `go.mod`). Key libraries (versions as in `go.mod`):
- `charm.land/bubbletea/v2` (v2.1.1) - TUI framework (v2: `tea.KeyPressMsg`, `tea.PasteMsg`, `View() tea.View`)
- `charm.land/bubbles/v2` (v2.2.1) - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, viewport)

- `github.com/NimbleMarkets/ntcharts/v2` (v2.9.0) - dashboard sparkline

- `github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` - which interface a destination leaves by, on all three platforms (§3.44)
- `golang.org/x/sys` - direct (Rule 303): the socket calls of `internal/nettrace` (`IP_TTL`, `IP_RECVERR`, `recvmsg` on the error queue); `x/sys/windows` serves `iphlpapi` (the Windows path trace, `IcmpSendEcho2`)
- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Views render through `Render()`** (Bubble Tea v2): a top-level view implements
`Render() string` and `View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }`; only the
router (`App.View()`) sets terminal state such as `AltScreen` and `BackgroundColor`. Components keep
`View() string`. Colours are `color.Color`; hex literals stay in `theme/colors.go`.

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |

| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135, 140 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment, invalid field |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (loading or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`), for a view's own load as well as for work the router tracks. The braille spinner API is removed (DEVDESK-377): nothing under `internal/` imports `bubbles/v2/spinner` or names `Status.Spinner`, `SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` or `theme.SpinnerStyle` (`TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner`, `TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone`), with no exception. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a loading screen or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

### 1.1 Fixed

**D157 — DEVDESK-504 (NX-01): a disposable Nexus Community bench on the datomir k0s cluster, driven by a Go tool outside `ci`. Decided (user, 2026-11-16, plan `.claude/plans/DEVDESK-504-plan.md`, drafted there under this number): (1) The tool is `internal/nexusbench` with its command `cmd/nexus-bench`, reached only through the tasks `nexus-bench:up`, `provision`, `down`, `status`, `render` and `test` of `mise.toml`. None is reachable from `ci`, `check`, `test` or `test-race`, and `mise_tasks_test.go` checks it. Each task declares kubectl `1.35` itself, not in the global `[tools]`; `render` contacts no cluster and declares none. (2) kubectl is driven as a process (`kubectl.go`), not through `client-go`. (3) Manifests are embedded `text/template` files, with the values validated before rendering. The namespace is `nexus-bench`, the NodePorts are 30481 (REST and UI) and 30482 (Docker connector), and 30483-30489 stays reserved for the next NX stories. (4) The descriptor is a versioned JSON file, `internal/nexusbench/descriptor.json`, written deterministically; it holds no secret. (5) Secrets stay out of the repository, in `$XDG_STATE_HOME/devdesk/nexus-bench/` (else `~/.local/state`, else the path given by `NEXUS_BENCH_SECRETS`), outside the worktrees' reach and refused inside the repository (`secrets.go`). (6) REST credentials are sent to `127.0.0.1` by default. Another host needs `--rest-host`, and the command then warns that the credentials travel in clear text. (7) The Community EULA is accepted only when the operator sets `NEXUS_BENCH_ACCEPT_EULA=yes` (or `--accept-eula`); the REST client never accepts it on its own. (8) Destruction deletes the one namespace the tool labelled; `down` leaves the descriptor alone. (9) Integration tests are gated: `DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH=1` for the read-only tests, and additionally `DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH_LIFECYCLE=1` with `NEXUS_BENCH_ACCEPT_EULA=yes` for the destructive lifecycle; `nexus-bench:test` runs with `-timeout 60m`, and the lifecycle refuses to start with less than 45 minutes left. Measured on `datomir` (k0s v1.36, Nexus 3.98.1-01 Community) on 2026-11-16: the read-only tests and the lifecycle pass (lifecycle 151 s); a first `up` is Ready in 48 s; a second and third `up` are idempotent (no `POST` beyond the refused proxy, the same `descriptor.json` byte for byte). **Measured change, proxy deferred to NX-02:** Nexus refuses (`400`, `Proxy URL blocked: Failed to resolve host`) a Docker proxy whose upstream host does not resolve, and `bench-upstream` does not exist before NX-02. The bench therefore ships without `docker-proxy`, and `docker-group` holds `docker-hosted` alone. The versioned `descriptor.json` describes that state and differs from the one NX-02 will write (proxy present and listed in the group). Rejected: (a) bash scripts (not testable as units in this repository); (b) `client-go` (weight in the binary's `go.mod`); (c) ignoring the descriptor in git (NX-08 could no longer detect a changed version without the bench). Consequences: NX-02 deploys the upstream `bench-upstream` (port 5000) and a NodePort of the reserved block, then re-runs `mise run nexus-bench:up`, checks that `docker-proxy` exists and is in `docker-group`, and commits the new `descriptor.json`; NX-03 to NX-08 read the descriptor through `nexusbench.LoadDescriptor`. Residual risks, accepted for a throw-away bench, not fixed here (`docs/architecture/nexus-bench.md`, "Residual risks"): the Basic credentials travel in clear HTTP; the `local-path` data folder is `0777`, so `admin.password` is readable by every local account of the node until the password is changed; the NodePorts listen on every interface of the node with anonymous access on by default; the image tag is mutable (no digest pinned). Not addressed by this decision: the precondition of the namespace deletion beyond the label check, and the mutable tag pinned by digest; both belong to NX-02 or later. **Plane:** DEVDESK-504 (story), DEVDESK-533 (NX-01). Sources: `.claude/plans/DEVDESK-504-plan.md`, `docs/architecture/nexus-bench.md` (decisions D-B and following, "The command and the mise tasks", "Integration tests and source guards", "First real run", "Residual risks"), `internal/nexusbench/params.go`, `secrets.go`, `descriptor.json`; D156 is not related.**
